notes: The Netherlands' dominant work route — sponsor-driven with no labour market test, closest structural equivalent to UK Skilled Worker and Germany's EU Blue Card/general skilled-worker permits. Three salary bands confirmed directly from ind.nl: €5,942 (30+), €4,357 (under 30), €3,122 (reduced/graduate) — all gross/month EXCLUDING the 8% holiday allowance, which is the IND's own standard framing and a genuinely distinctive Dutch convention worth surfacing prominently, since third-party sites sometimes quote annual or holiday-allowance-inclusive figures that don't match. Live counterfeit-figure risk confirmed during research: multiple tier-3 sites showing prior-year figures (€2,801-€2,989 for the reduced rate, ~€4,752 for under-30) as if current for 2026 — same pattern as every other country in this dataset. FORMULA MODELING DECLINED DELIBERATELY: these thresholds ARE indexed annually (1 January) and the reduced/family/PR 'required amounts' also index a second time on 1 July, but IND does not publish them as an explicit ratio of a named reference variable the way Germany's Blue Card threshold is stated as a percentage of the pension ceiling — so encoding a formula_ref/ratio here would mean fabricating a relationship not actually confirmed at tier-1 precision. Literal values with a clear annual re-verification flag is the honest choice. citizenship_after_months set equal to pr_after_months (60) since NL naturalisation's standard residence requirement is also 5 years and PR is typically the qualifying status — dual_citizenship_allowed is false as the GENERAL rule (see nl_naturalisation for the real exemption list, which is substantial).
